examples.title: Vermilion flycatcher
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Camera-recorded focus distance is approximate.
examples.note: The bird and nest hold fine detail while branches at other distances soften. A long lens and a wide aperture help isolate this small subject.

details.label: Bird & nest
details.note: Inspect the feathers and woven nest. Focus selects a distance; it does not make every branch equally sharp.

details.label: Soft branches
details.note: Overlapping blur disks soften branches beyond the focus distance. Enlarging this region shows recorded defocus, not missing download detail.

examples.title: Mallard and ducklings
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Camera-recorded focus distance is approximate.
examples.note: Compare the ducklings, the log and the water. Objects at similar distances can share the sharp region even when they are different subjects.

details.label: Duckling detail
details.note: Down and bark reveal small-scale texture. A shallow focus zone does not make every animal equally sharp.

details.label: Water highlights
details.note: Reflections spread into soft shapes. Defocus and water motion can both affect them; a single image cannot separate those effects precisely.

examples.title: Fox beside the snow
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Camera-recorded focus distance is approximate.
examples.note: The fox stands between snow and soft distant scenery. The recorded 1/1000-second exposure limits motion during capture; focus and scene depth shape the remaining softness.

details.label: Fox detail
details.note: Compare facial detail with the softer fur farther from the focus plane. The photograph alone cannot establish which softness came from motion or defocus.

details.label: Snow edge
details.note: The snow and rock create bright boundaries. Bright areas can lose detail if their signal clips, but this crop is not a RAW clipping measurement.

examples.title: Ground squirrel on a rock
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Camera-recorded focus distance is approximate.
examples.note: The squirrel and textured rock stand against a smooth background. ISO 2000 amplifies the captured signal; it does not create additional photons.

details.label: Eye & fur
details.note: Inspect the eye and the fine hairs. Fine detail depends on focus, lens blur, captured light and the processing already applied to this JPEG.

details.label: Smooth background
details.note: Broad color gradients replace distant detail. This is the captured background, not an artificial blur effect added by the app.

examples.title: Fox portrait
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: The face stands out against a soft backdrop. The edited file retains aperture, shutter and ISO, but no recorded focus distance.

details.label: Face & whiskers
details.note: Look closely at the eyes, muzzle and whiskers. The crop uses the supplied portrait, including any editing already applied.

details.label: Fur texture
details.note: Hair texture changes across the depth of the body. We cannot recover the original focus distance or sharpening choices from this JPEG.

examples.title: Sheep in the mountain valley
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: A 50 mm view includes both the flock and the mountain setting. At f/1.8, depth of field remains limited even though the wider view makes the landscape recognizable.

details.label: Foreground sheep
details.note: Compare the horns, wool and grass. Recognizable detail is not a calibrated measure of depth of field.

details.label: Mountain backdrop
details.note: The mountains establish the setting while their fine edges appear softer. Their actual distance and the original focus distance were not supplied.

examples.title: Curly-coated sheep
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: The close composition emphasizes curls and a dark face. The supplied file records a 500 mm lens; the portrait framing also reflects the supplied crop.

details.label: Face & curls
details.note: The pale curls surround darker facial detail. Exposure and processing determine how much texture remains in bright and dark areas.

details.label: Wool detail
details.note: Individual curls contain high-frequency detail. This enlargement comes from the full-resolution source rather than the small gallery preview.

examples.title: Horned sheep portrait
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: The horns and face stand out against a green hillside. The long lens and scene geometry separate the subject from its surroundings; focus distance is unavailable.

details.label: Horns & face
details.note: Compare the horn edges with the wool and eyes. Sharpness can change across different depths of the animal.

details.label: Soft hillside
details.note: The hillside becomes broad green shapes. A sharp subject and soft background can coexist because they occupy different distances.

examples.title: Chipmunk above the rocks
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: The small animal is framed by textured rock and a quiet background. A 1/320-second exposure gathers more light than a faster shutter at the same aperture, but leaves more opportunity for motion blur.

details.label: Face & stripes
details.note: The eye, whiskers and stripes give useful fine-detail targets. This is a crop of the new portrait source.

details.label: Rock texture
details.note: The rocks show detail at nearby distances. The JPEG records the combined effects of optics, motion and processing.

examples.title: Bears on the riverbank
examples.credit: Photo: Reed Osaki. Focus distance was not retained in the supplied file.
examples.note: The nearer bear and the second bear occupy different depths. This photograph was recorded with a Canon EOS Rebel T7 and a 75–300 mm lens at 160 mm; that lens is not in the simulator.

details.label: Near bear
details.note: Inspect the face and coat of the nearer bear. This crop uses the supplied Canon photograph, not the simulator’s Nikon camera model.

details.label: Second bear
details.note: Compare the smaller bear with the foreground subject. Subject distance and image size both affect how much visible detail it contains.
